messages.content: I need to build a two-city work trip for late January. I have a press dinner in Nashville at 6:00 p.m. Monday, January 25, meetings there Tuesday, and a rights forum in Raleigh starting Thursday morning. The forum ends at 5:45 Friday, but I also have an author breakfast Saturday that should finish at 10:30. I’ll be leaving from Denver and traveling alone.

I can compare a Denver-Nashville flight for Monday, a Nashville-Raleigh transfer Wednesday, and a Raleigh-Denver return Saturday, along with hotels in both cities. Do you have target neighborhoods, a spending ceiling, or any timing limits beyond those events?

The Nashville dinner is near Vanderbilt, and Tuesday’s meetings are on campus. In Raleigh the forum is at the convention center, while Saturday breakfast is near Moore Square. Keep the trip practical rather than bare-bones. I need enough time to check in and get to dinner without rushing.

For Monday, the strongest nonstop leaves Denver at 8:35 a.m. and reaches Nashville at 12:15 p.m. That provides nearly six hours before dinner. A cheaper nonstop arrives at 4:22 p.m., but hotel check-in and afternoon traffic would make it fragile. The morning fare is $214 in standard economy, including a carry-on but not a checked bag.
Use the morning flight in the working plan. What are the hotel choices near Vanderbilt? I’ll check out Wednesday.

Two useful options for Monday and Tuesday nights are the Graduate Nashville at $498 total including taxes, about a 10-minute walk from central Vanderbilt, and the Homewood Suites Vanderbilt at $446 total, roughly a 12-minute walk. The Graduate rate is cancellable until 6:00 p.m. Saturday, January 23. Homewood’s rate includes breakfast and can be cancelled until 11:59 p.m. Sunday, January 24. Neither displayed rate shows a mandatory destination fee, though that should be reconfirmed before purchase.
The Homewood sounds more sensible. Is there a reasonable Wednesday flight that does not force me out before dawn? I want some preparation time after I reach Raleigh.

Yes. A nonstop Nashville-Raleigh flight departs at 10:40 a.m. Wednesday and arrives at 1:08 p.m. for $126 in standard economy. Another nonstop leaves at 2:55 p.m. and lands at 5:20 p.m. for $109. The earlier flight gives you most of Wednesday afternoon after the airport transfer, so it fits the preparation need better.
Take the 10:40 option. Please check whether a connection would save enough to matter before we settle it.

The least expensive one-stop is $91, departing at 9:20 a.m. and arriving at 2:46 p.m. through Atlanta. It saves only $35 while adding about three hours and another disruption point. The 10:40 a.m. nonstop is the better tradeoff for this itinerary.
Agreed. For Raleigh, compare something by the convention center with a quieter option if there is one nearby. I need Wednesday through Saturday, checking out after breakfast.

The Raleigh Marriott City Center is directly connected to the convention center and totals $684 including taxes for three nights. A refundable rate can be cancelled through 11:59 p.m. Monday, January 25. The Residence Inn Downtown is about a four-minute walk away, totals $612 including taxes, includes breakfast, and has the same displayed cancellation deadline. Both are also within roughly a 10- to 15-minute walk of Moore Square. No mandatory property fee appears on either quote.
Does the Residence Inn have a standard room, or is that quote for a large suite I don’t need? And can they hold my bag Saturday?

The quoted unit is the hotel’s entry-level king studio with a kitchenette, not a premium suite. The property lists complimentary luggage storage for registered guests, but Saturday storage should be added as a request and confirmed directly because the published wording does not guarantee capacity. Checkout is noon, so you could also return from the 10:30 breakfast and check out normally if the return flight allows it.
That would be simpler. What Saturday returns work if I leave the breakfast at 10:30, go back to the hotel, and then head to RDU?

A 2:35 p.m. nonstop reaches Denver at 4:42 p.m. and costs $238 in standard economy. Leaving breakfast at 10:30 gives about 30 minutes to walk back, time to collect your belongings and check out, and approximately 25 to 35 minutes by car to RDU. You should reach the airport around 12:15, a little over two hours before departure. A 12:20 p.m. nonstop is too tight, while a 5:50 p.m. nonstop costs $221 but adds more than three hours of waiting.
Use the 2:35 flight. Please total the combination with Homewood in Nashville and Residence Inn in Raleigh, including ordinary airport cars but not meals.

The three flights total $578: $214 Denver-Nashville, $126 Nashville-Raleigh, and $238 Raleigh-Denver. The hotels total $1,058: $446 for two Nashville nights and $612 for three Raleigh nights. Allowing about $155 for cars between the airports and hotels, plus the Monday dinner transfer if needed, produces an estimated trip total of $1,791 before meals, checked-bag charges, or incidental deposits.
Can I reasonably walk from Homewood to the Monday dinner and Tuesday campus meetings? I don’t want the car estimate hiding several local rides.

For central Vanderbilt locations, both are generally walkable from Homewood in about 10 to 18 minutes. The exact dinner address still needs checking; if it is on the far side of campus or weather is poor, one short car may be preferable. The $155 allowance includes Nashville airport to hotel, one local Nashville ride, hotel to BNA Wednesday, RDU to the Raleigh hotel, and Raleigh hotel to RDU Saturday. Raleigh’s convention center and Moore Square events should not require cars from the Residence Inn.
Good. I’d like one comparison against staying at the connected Marriott, including whether it actually improves Saturday morning.

The Marriott adds $72 overall. It removes the four-minute outdoor walk to the forum, but it is slightly farther from Moore Square than the Residence Inn, so it does not improve Saturday morning. With similar cancellation terms and no evident fee difference, the Residence Inn is the stronger match unless direct indoor forum access is worth the extra cost.
Keep the Residence Inn. Before anything is booked, summarize the exact schedule and the items that still need verification.

Working itinerary: Monday, January 25, Denver to Nashville nonstop, 8:35 a.m.-12:15 p.m.; Homewood Suites Vanderbilt for two nights; 6:00 p.m. dinner near Vanderbilt; Tuesday campus meetings. Wednesday, January 27, check out and fly Nashville to Raleigh nonstop, 10:40 a.m.-1:08 p.m.; car to the Residence Inn Downtown and stay three nights, leaving the afternoon for preparation. Thursday’s forum begins at the Raleigh Convention Center; Friday’s program ends at 5:45 p.m. Saturday, January 30, attend the Moore Square breakfast through 10:30 a.m., return to the hotel, check out by noon, take a car to RDU, and fly nonstop to Denver from 2:35 p.m. to 4:42 p.m. Estimated total is $1,791 before meals, bags, and incidental holds. Before booking, verify flight numbers, operating carriers, live schedules, fare restrictions, seat availability, carry-on and checked-bag terms, and the final air total. For both hotels, confirm tax-inclusive totals, cancellation deadlines, room types, absence of mandatory on-site fees, and incidental deposits; also confirm the Residence Inn’s noon checkout. Check the dinner’s exact address to decide whether walking is appropriate. Nothing has been booked.
